about: Built-in embodiment cards (llm_card.py). A client may send one of these names as "embodiment", or nothing when its request has the card's keys. The frames and image directions of libero_franka were measured in vla-eval's LIBERO images (rotated 180 degrees from robosuite's render, as openpi's LIBERO example does) and hold for the tabletop scenes: libero_spatial, libero_goal and libero_10's kitchen scenes; libero_object (a floor scene) and libero_10's study and living-room scenes put the table elsewhere.

cards.name: libero_franka
cards.docs:
One Franka Panda arm with a parallel-jaw gripper on a fixed base, simulated at 20 control steps per second. World frame in metres: +z is up; the robot base stands at about x = -0.66, y = 0 and reaches forward along +x. The table top is at about z = 0.90; the lowest the grasp point can go is z = 0.91. The grasp point (between the two finger pads) reaches at most 0.75 m horizontally from the base axis. The bounds below are the reachable workspace.
move_to takes the grasp point's x, y, z, the hand's orientation as rot6d (the first two columns of its rotation matrix in the world frame: r00, r10, r20, then r01, r11, r21) and the gripper command, 0 open and 1 closed. The hand starts pointing straight down with the jaws opening along world y. Leave r00 to r21 unnamed to keep the orientation. To turn the hand about the vertical by an angle t, rotate both columns about z: each column (cx, cy, cz) becomes (cx cos t - cy sin t, cx sin t + cy cos t, cz); a quarter turn makes the jaws open along world x. The jaws open about 8 cm.
Time: the hand moves at most about 1.2 cm per control step, so a 20 cm move takes about 20 steps. After each motion the arm keeps tracking its last target until it is within 5 mm and 2 degrees or stops making progress, and a gripper change gets about 12 more steps, before you see the next observation. The step budget in each observation counts every control step, so the time left is the steps left divided by 20, in seconds. Several axes in one move cost no more steps than the longest of them.
State: eef_state is x, y, z, the six rot6d values and the gripper command. gripper_qpos holds the two finger positions (about +0.04 and -0.04 when fully open, near 0 when closed on nothing): fingers that stopped apart after closing mean that something is between them. A target the arm cannot reach shows as a remaining offset from the setpoint.
Cameras: agentview is a third-person camera facing the robot across the table, the robot at the top of the image; world +x points toward the bottom of the image and world +y toward the LEFT. wrist is a camera on the hand looking down; at the start orientation world +x points toward the top of this image and +y toward the right, and the image turns with the hand. The fingertips show as dark shapes at its bottom edge; a point on the table directly under the grasp point shows horizontally centred, about 60% of the way down. Near the table 1 cm is about 5 pixels of the 224-pixel wrist image. There is no depth image and no object-position query: estimate positions from the images.
A held object hangs below the grasp point. The episode ends by itself when the task is done or the step budget runs out; you cannot declare success.
